mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In an early recovery regime characterized by rising industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 tends to generate positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days as manufacturing activity expands and corporate profits improve.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising in the early recovery phase, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 6.0%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 6.0%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening monetary policy amid a strong labor market, which typically precedes economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market strength
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500 thousand units, it indicates a contraction in the housing sector that reduces consumer wealth and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1500, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
